title: Darood Sharif, Ruhani Ilaj, Duas and Azkar
description: Four libraries from the Qur'an and Sunnah. Each wording stays in its own section, with Arabic, a reading, the meaning, when to say it, and the reference.
review_note: A reminder drawn from the Qur'an and hadith collections. It is not a fatwa and not medical advice. Ruhani Ilaj here means ruqyah: recitation and dua, with the cure asked from Allah. Talismans, jinn invocation, and fortune-telling are outside this catalog. A qualified scholar reviews rulings. A doctor treats illness.

privacy.storage: Saved texts, today's recital marks, and the daily counter stay on this device. They are not encrypted and are not a backup. The catalog cache is kept for offline reading. No account, journal, or analytics is written by this screen.

sections.title: Darood Sharif
sections.summary: Salawat upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the wordings taught in the Qur'an and sound hadith, plus one composed salawat that is clearly labeled.
intro: Allah commanded the believers to send salah and salam upon the Prophet ﷺ. The Companions asked him how to do it, and he taught them the words. Those words are the heart of this section.
A reward narrated for salawat belongs to salawat upon him, not to a private formula. Composed salawat can be a humble dua, and this library marks them so they are never mistaken for his wording.

Schools differ on whether the Ibrahimic salawat inside the tashahhud is a pillar, an obligation, or an emphasized sunnah. This page does not settle that. Follow the teacher whose fiqh you pray behind.

sections.title: Ruhani Ilaj
sections.summary: Spiritual treatment in the Sunnah is ruqyah: Qur'an and dua, with the cure asked from Allah. It is not magic, not a talisman, and not a substitute for a doctor.
intro: Ruhani Ilaj on this page means ruqyah shar'iyyah. You recite the Qur'an and the duas he ﷺ recited, you blow lightly, and you ask Allah to heal. The words do not heal by themselves. Allah heals.

Three limits keep a ruqyah inside Islam. It uses Allah's words or His names, in wording you understand. It does not call on a jinn, a star, a saint, or a dead person. And the heart knows the cure is from Allah alone. Ibn Hajar recorded these limits from the scholars in Fath al-Bari.

See a doctor for illness. The Prophet ﷺ said to seek treatment, because Allah did not send down a disease without sending down its cure. Ruqyah sits beside medicine. It does not replace it. Serious fear, voices, or a collapse of ordinary life also needs a qualified clinician, not only a recitation.

sections.title: Duas
sections.summary: Supplications from the Qur'an and the duas the Prophet ﷺ taught. Dhikr with a fixed daily count lives in Azkar. Salawat lives in Darood Sharif. Healing ruqyah lives in Ruhani Ilaj.
intro: A dua is asking Allah. The best words are the ones He taught in the Qur'an and the ones His Messenger ﷺ taught. Your own words, in any language, are also dua, as long as you ask Allah alone and you do not ask for a sin or the cutting of family.
Praise Allah and send salawat before you ask. That order is in the Darood section, from the hadith of Fudalah ibn Ubayd. This section keeps the asking itself.

Nothing here is a bargain. Allah answers by giving what was asked, or by turning away a harm, or by storing it for the next life. That is the meaning of the hadith that the dua of a Muslim is answered as long as he does not ask for sin or the severing of kinship.

sections.title: Azkar
sections.summary: The remembrances of the morning, the evening, the prayer, sleep, and the day. Each one stays a dhikr: a wording to repeat, with the count when the Sunnah gave a count.
intro: Azkar are the words of remembrance repeated at known times. The morning set is after Fajr until sunrise is the best window, and it remains morning remembrance until before Dhuhr. The evening set begins after Asr and is especially fitting after Maghrib.

Where a count is on the card, that count is the one in the report. Where scholars differed on the chain, the card says so. Reciting the Qur'an is worship even when a particular virtue-report is discussed.
The counter on this page is only a private aid for today. It clears on the next calendar day. It does not replace presence of heart.

items.title: The command to send salah and salam
items.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلَائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ۚ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا
items.transliteration: Inna Allaha wa mala'ikatahu yusalluna alan-nabi. Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu sallu alayhi wa sallimu taslima.
items.meaning: Indeed, Allah and His angels send salah upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send salah upon him and greet him with a complete salam.
items.when: This is the verse the practice rests on. Recite it, then send salawat in the words he taught.
items.virtue: Scholars explain salah from Allah as praise and mercy, salah from the angels as dua, and salah from the believers as the supplication he taught.

items.title: Durood Ibrahim, the fuller wording
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ala Ibrahima wa ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid. Allahumma barik ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ala Ibrahima wa ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent salah upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, send blessing upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent blessing upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
items.when: In the tashahhud of the prayer, and whenever a person wants the salawat he himself taught. Ka'b ibn Ujrah reported that the Companions asked, after they already knew the salam, how they should send salah.
items.virtue: This is the gift Ka'b ibn Ujrah passed on. Both this fuller wording and the next shorter one are in Sahih al-Bukhari.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 3370; also Sahih Muslim, from Ka'b ibn Ujrah

items.title: Durood Ibrahim, the shorter wording
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid. Allahumma barik ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent salah upon the family of Ibrahim. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed the family of Ibrahim. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
items.when: A second authentic wording of the same teaching. Either wording he taught is sound to say in the tashahhud.
items.virtue: The Prophet ﷺ called this the answer when they asked how to send salah upon him.

items.title: Salawat upon him, his wives, and his descendants
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَأَزْوَاجِهِ وَذُرِّيَّتِهِ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَبَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَأَزْوَاجِهِ وَذُرِّيَّتِهِ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa azwajihi wa dhurriyyatihi kama sallayta ala ali Ibrahim, wa barik ala Muhammadin wa azwajihi wa dhurriyyatihi kama barakta ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants as You sent salah upon the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad, his wives, and his descendants as You blessed the family of Ibrahim. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
items.when: Taught when the Companions asked again how to send salah. It is recited as salawat, including by people who use it in the prayer.
items.virtue: It names the wives and the descendants inside the family he loved.

items.title: One salawat, and Allah sends ten
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad.
items.when: A short salawat in the meaning of the command. The ten-count here is only a small daily practice, not a number he fixed for this short sentence.
items.virtue: When you hear the mu'adhdhin, repeat what he says, then send salah upon the Prophet ﷺ. Whoever sends one salah upon him, Allah sends salah upon that person ten times. Then ask Allah for al-Wasilah for him.

items.title: Increase salawat on Friday
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ala Ibrahima wa ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent salah upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
items.when: Friday, and the night that precedes it. Use the same salawat he taught. The day is not tied to a secret number.
items.virtue: Aws ibn Aws reported: the best of your days is Friday, so send more salah upon me that day, for your salah is presented to me. The Companions asked how, after his death. He said Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1047, hadith of Aws ibn Aws

items.title: The people closest to him on the Last Day
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli wa sallim ala nabiyyina Muhammad.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah and salam upon our Prophet Muhammad.
items.when: Any time of the day. This short sentence is a respectful salawat. The hadith does not fix these exact syllables, and it does not fix a magic count.
items.virtue: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the people closest to him on the Day of Resurrection are those who sent the most salah upon him.
items.reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 484. At-Tirmidhi graded it hasan.

items.title: Angels carry the salawat of the Ummah
items.arabic: صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
items.transliteration: Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
items.meaning: May Allah send salah and salam upon him.
items.when: Whenever his name is mentioned, and whenever you write it.
items.virtue: Allah has angels who travel the earth and convey to the Prophet ﷺ the salam of his Ummah. A separate hadith calls the person who hears him mentioned and does not send salah a miser.
items.reference: Musnad Ahmad and Sunan an-Nasa'i, the roaming angels; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3546 on the miser, graded hasan

items.title: When the whole dua is salawat
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama sallayta ala Ibrahima wa ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid. Allahumma barik ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad, kama barakta ala Ibrahima wa ala ali Ibrahim, innaka Hamidun Majid.
items.meaning: The Ibrahimic salawat, in full.
items.when: Ubayy ibn Ka'b asked how much of his personal dua should be salawat. The Prophet ﷺ said: as much as you wish. Ubayy offered a quarter, then a half, then two thirds, then all of it.
items.virtue: He said: then your needs will be sufficed, and your sins will be forgiven. Filling a dua with salawat does not cancel asking Allah for lawful needs. It teaches the rank of salawat.
items.reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2457; Musnad Ahmad, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b

items.title: Praise Allah, then salawat, then ask
items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ
items.transliteration: Alhamdu lillah, wassalatu wassalamu ala Rasulillah. Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad.
items.meaning: Praise belongs to Allah, and salah and salam upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
items.when: Begin a personal dua this way, then ask for what you need. The first line is the order he described. The salawat sentence is the short form of what he taught.
items.virtue: He heard a man make dua without praising Allah and without salawat, and he said the man was hasty. Then he taught: praise Allah, send salah upon the Prophet ﷺ, then ask.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1481; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3477, from Fudalah ibn Ubayd

items.title: Salawat when the adhan is called
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ هَذِهِ الدَّعْوَةِ التَّامَّةِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْقَائِمَةِ، آتِ مُحَمَّدًا الْوَسِيلَةَ وَالْفَضِيلَةَ، وَابْعَثْهُ مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا الَّذِي وَعَدْتَهُ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli wa sallim ala Muhammad. Allahumma Rabba hadhihid-da'watit-tammah wassalatil-qa'imah, ati Muhammadanil-wasilata wal-fadilah, wab'athhu maqaman mahmuda nilladhi wa'adtah.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah and salam upon Muhammad. O Allah, Lord of this complete call and of the prayer that is about to be established, give Muhammad the Wasilah and excellence, and raise him to the praised station You promised him.
items.when: After repeating the adhan. Send salawat first, then ask for al-Wasilah. The Wasilah sentence is the wording in Sahih al-Bukhari. Some later reports add 'You do not break Your promise.'
items.virtue: Whoever asks the Wasilah for him after the adhan receives the promise of his intercession, as in Sahih Muslim 384.
items.reference: Sahih Muslim 384 for the order; Sahih al-Bukhari 614 for the Wasilah dua

items.title: Durood Tunajjina, a composed salawat
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَاةً تُنْجِينَا بِهَا مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْأَهْوَالِ وَالْآفَاتِ، وَتَقْضِي لَنَا بِهَا جَمِيعَ الْحَاجَاتِ، وَتُطَهِّرُنَا بِهَا مِنْ جَمِيعِ السَّيِّئَاتِ، وَتَرْفَعُنَا بِهَا أَعْلَى الدَّرَجَاتِ، وَتُبَلِّغُنَا بِهَا أَقْصَى الْغَايَاتِ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْخَيْرَاتِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ وَبَعْدَ الْمَمَاتِ
items.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala sayyidina Muhammad, salatan tunajjina biha min jami'il-ahwali wal-afat, wa taqdi lana biha jami'al-hajat, wa tutahhiruna biha min jami'is-sayyi'at, wa tarfa'una biha a'lad-darajat, wa tuballighuna biha aqsal-ghayati min jami'il-khayrati fil-hayati wa ba'dal-mamati.
items.meaning: O Allah, send salah upon our master Muhammad, a salah by which You save us from every terror and harm, fulfill for us every need, purify us from every sin, raise us to the highest degrees, and carry us to the furthest goals of every good in life and after death.
items.when: A personal salawat many Muslims recite. It is not a wording reported from the Prophet ﷺ, and it is not said inside the tashahhud in place of the Ibrahimic salawat.
items.virtue: Sending salah upon him in respectful words is allowed. Do not attach a specific hadith reward, a fixed count such as a lakh, or a guaranteed outcome to this composition. The virtues above belong to the authentic reports.
items.reference: Composed salawat, widely recited. Not in the Sahih collections as his wording. Kept here so it is not confused with Durood Ibrahim.
items.note: Tasawwuf in this library means adab and sincerity. It does not turn a composed poem into a hadith.

items.title: When I am ill, He heals me
items.arabic: وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ
items.transliteration: Wa idha maridtu fa-Huwa yashfin.
items.meaning: And when I am ill, it is He who heals me.
items.when: Say it as Ibrahim said it: healing is Allah's act. Doctors, medicine, and ruqyah are means He created.
items.virtue: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, counted this among the favors of the Lord of the worlds.

items.title: The Qur'an is a healing
items.arabic: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
items.transliteration: Wa nunazzilu minal-Qur'ani ma huwa shifa'un wa rahmatun lil-mu'minin.
items.meaning: And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers.
items.when: Any sincere recitation is a means of healing, especially for what is in the chest. A second verse calls the revelation a healing for what is in the breasts: Qur'an 10:57.
items.virtue: The healing is for the believers. It is not a product that works by a secret count.

items.title: Seek treatment
items.arabic: تَدَاوَوْا، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَمْ يَضَعْ دَاءً إِلَّا وَضَعَ لَهُ دَوَاءً، غَيْرَ دَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ: الْهَرَمُ
items.transliteration: Tadawaw, fa-inna Allaha azza wa jalla lam yada' da'an illa wada'a lahu dawa'an, ghayra da'in wahid: al-haram.
items.meaning: Seek treatment. Allah has not sent down a disease except that He has also sent down its cure, except for one condition: old age.
items.when: Before you begin ruqyah for a sickness, take the medical path that is open to you. Then recite. Do not delay an emergency for a recitation.
items.virtue: A related wording in Sahih al-Bukhari says Allah did not send a disease without sending its cure.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 3855; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2038. The Bukhari wording: Sahih al-Bukhari 5678

items.title: Whoever can benefit his brother should do so
items.arabic: مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَنْفَعَ أَخَاهُ فَلْيَفْعَلْ
items.transliteration: Man istata'a minkum an yanfa'a akhahu fal-yaf'al.
items.meaning: Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so.
items.when: When you recite ruqyah for someone with Qur'an and a dua you understand. The context was a scorpion sting, after he had first restricted ruqyah and then allowed the kind that is a real benefit.
items.virtue: Ruqyah with the Qur'an is a service, not a performance and not a secret trade.

items.title: Al-Fatihah is a ruqyah
items.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
items.transliteration: Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. Alhamdu lillahi Rabbil-alamin. Ar-Rahmanir-Rahim. Maliki yawmid-din. Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in. Ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim. Siratalladhina an'amta alayhim ghayril-maghdubi alayhim wa lad-dallin.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who earned anger, nor of those who went astray.
items.when: Recite it over the sick person, or over yourself, and blow lightly. The Companion who treated a sting recited Umm al-Qur'an. Seven times is a widespread practice drawn from the reports of repeating a ruqyah. The hadith itself establishes al-Fatihah as a ruqyah. It does not sell a guaranteed count.
items.virtue: The Prophet ﷺ smiled and said: how did you know it is a ruqyah? Take the payment, and set aside a share for me. Paying or accepting a simple fee for Qur'anic ruqyah has this precedent. Selling fear does not.

items.title: Ayat al-Kursi as protection
items.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
items.transliteration: Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum. La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm. Lahu ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard. Man dhalladhi yashfa'u indahu illa bi-idhnih. Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum. Wa la yuhituna bi-shay'in min ilmihi illa bima sha'. Wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samawati wal-ard. Wa la ya'uduhu hifdhuhuma. Wa Huwal-Aliyyul-Azim.
items.meaning: Allah, there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them. They do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and guarding them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
items.when: Recite it over yourself and over the one you are treating. Recite it before sleep and after the obligatory prayers. Those are the sunnah places of this verse.
items.virtue: A protector from Allah remains, and shaytan does not come near until morning, when it is read before sleep.

items.title: The Mu'awwidhat for illness
items.arabic:
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ۝ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ۝ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ۝ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
items.transliteration: Qul Huwallahu Ahad. Allahus-Samad. Lam yalid wa lam yulad. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad. Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbil-falaq. Min sharri ma khalaq. Wa min sharri ghasqin idha waqab. Wa min sharrin-naffathati fil-uqad. Wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad. Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbin-nas. Malikin-nas. Ilahin-nas. Min sharril-waswasil-khannas. Alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas. Minal-jinnati wan-nas.
items.meaning: Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He does not beget and was not begotten, and there is none equal to Him. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He created, from the darkness when it settles, from those who blow on knots, and from an envier when he envies. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers in the chests of people, among jinn and mankind.
items.when: Cup the hands, recite the three surahs, blow lightly, and wipe the body. Aishah did this for him when he was ill, using his own hand because of its blessing. For someone else, recite and blow lightly toward them, or into your hands and wipe if they are a person you may touch, such as your own child or spouse.
items.virtue: When he was ill he would recite the Mu'awwidhat, blow, and wipe himself. When his illness grew heavy, Aishah recited them over him.

items.title: The last two verses of al-Baqarah at night
items.arabic:
آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۚ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ ۚ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ

لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ ۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ ۖ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا ۚ أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
items.transliteration: Amanar-Rasulu bima unzila ilayhi mir-Rabbihi wal-mu'minun. Kullun amana billahi wa mala'ikatihi wa kutubihi wa rusulih. La nufarriqu bayna ahadin mir-rusulih. Wa qalu sami'na wa ata'na, ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir. La yukallifullahu nafsan illa wus'aha. Laha ma kasabat wa alayha maktasabat. Rabbana la tu'akhidhna in nasina aw akhta'na. Rabbana wa la tahmil alayna isran kama hamaltahu alalladhina min qablina. Rabbana wa la tuhammilna ma la taqata lana bih. Wa'fu anna waghfir lana warhamna. Anta mawlana fansurna alal-qawmil-kafirin.
items.meaning: The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. All of them believe in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. They say: we hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return. Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or err. Do not lay on us a burden like the one before us. Do not burden us beyond what we can bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against the people who reject the truth.
items.when: At night, for the house and for the person who is unwell. They are part of the night protection, not a numbered spell.
items.virtue: Whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him. Shaytan does not enter a house in which al-Baqarah is recited, in Sahih Muslim 780.

items.title: The dua of Yunus in distress
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minadh-dhalimin.
items.meaning: There is no god except You. Glory be to You. I have been among the wrongdoers.
items.when: In illness, fear, and grief. It is also in the Duas section. Here it is the ruqyah of a tight chest.
items.virtue: No Muslim calls with it except that Allah answers. The wording is Qur'an. The virtue-report is Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3505.

items.title: O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ، اشْفِهِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِي، لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
items.transliteration: Allahumma Rabban-nas, adhhibil-ba's, ishfihi wa Antash-Shafi, la shifa'a illa shifa'uk, shifa'an la yughadiru saqama.
items.meaning: O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm, heal him, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind.
items.when: Wipe the sick person with the right hand, if they are someone you may touch, and say this. For yourself, say ishfini in place of ishfihi. For a woman, say ishfiha. He used to treat members of his family this way.
items.virtue: This is his own ruqyah. It states the creed of healing in one sentence: there is no healing except Yours.

items.title: Seven times: I ask Allah the Magnificent to heal you
items.arabic: أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ رَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَ
items.transliteration: As'alullaha al-Azima Rabbal-arshil-azima an yashfiyak.
items.meaning: I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the magnificent Throne, to heal you.
items.when: When you visit a sick person who is not at the point of death. Say it seven times. If you are the one who is ill, a visitor says it for you. For yourself, ask in the Rabban-nas dua.
items.virtue: No Muslim visits a sick Muslim who is not yet in the throes of death and says this seven times, except that he is healed, unless his appointed time has come.
items.note: The exception is in the hadith itself. Healing has an appointed term. The dua is still said.

items.title: The hand on the place of pain
items.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، ثَلَاثًا.
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ، سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ
items.transliteration: Bismillah, three times. Then seven times: A'udhu billahi wa qudratihi min sharri ma ajidu wa uhadhir.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah. I seek refuge in Allah and in His power from the evil of what I find and of what I fear.
items.when: Place your hand on the place that hurts, say Bismillah three times, then say the refuge seven times. Uthman ibn Abi al-As complained of a pain he had felt since he became Muslim, and this is what he was taught.
items.virtue: A ruqyah for pain in the body, with a fixed count from Sahih Muslim.

items.title: In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُؤْذِيكَ، مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ أَوْ عَيْنِ حَاسِدٍ، اللَّهُ يَشْفِيكَ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ
items.transliteration: Bismillahi arqik, min kulli shay'in yu'dhik, min sharri kulli nafsin aw aynin hasid, Allahu yashfik, bismillahi arqik.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or the eye of an envier. May Allah heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you.
items.when: Jibril performed ruqyah on the Prophet ﷺ with these words when he was ill. Say them over a sick person.
items.virtue: The angel's ruqyah. It names harm, the evil soul, and the envious eye, and it still asks Allah to heal.

items.title: Protection for children
items.arabic: أُعِيذُكُمَا بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
items.transliteration: U'idhukuma bi-kalimatillahit-tammah, min kulli shaytanin wa hammah, wa min kulli aynin lammah.
items.meaning: I seek protection for the two of you in the perfect words of Allah, from every devil and poisonous creature, and from every envious eye.
items.when: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek this protection for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and he said Ibrahim used to seek the same protection for Isma'il and Ishaq. For one child, say u'idhuka. For a girl, the same phrase with the feminine kasrah is used by many teachers: u'idhuki. The meaning is seeking protection for the child.
items.virtue: A ruqyah for the evil eye and for harm, taught as the practice of Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

items.title: The perfect words, against created harm
items.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
items.transliteration: A'udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq.
items.meaning: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created.
items.when: Three times in the evening, and three times when you stop somewhere on a journey. It is also in Azkar because it is a daily dhikr. Here it is the ruqyah against stings, fear of a place, and general harm.
items.virtue: Nothing will harm him until he leaves that place. A man who was stung had left it unsaid.

items.title: The evil eye is real
items.arabic: الْعَيْنُ حَقٌّ
items.transliteration: Al-aynu haqq.
items.meaning: The evil eye is real.
items.when: If you fear you have looked at someone with envy, make dua for blessing for them: Allahumma barik. If you are asked to wash because of an eye you cast, wash. Do not answer the evil eye with a talisman.
items.virtue: If anything were to overtake the divine decree, the evil eye would. When you are asked to wash, wash. The cure on the one who was looked at is ruqyah, including al-Fatihah, the Mu'awwidhat, and the duas on this page.
items.note: Washing is the sunnah response of the person who cast the eye. This page does not turn that into a ritual to invent at home with written squares.

items.title: Magic is real, and the cure is not more magic
items.arabic:
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ … وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ …
items.transliteration: Recite al-Falaq and an-Nas in full, including 'and from the evil of those who blow on knots.'
items.meaning: Seek refuge from the women, or people, who blow on knots, and from the whisperer. The full surahs are in Azkar.
items.when: If you fear magic, recite the Mu'awwidhat, Ayat al-Kursi, and the healing duas. Keep your prayers. Go to a doctor if the body or the mind is unwell. Do not go to a magician to undo magic with magic.
items.virtue: A spell was worked on the Prophet ﷺ. He refused a counter-spell, nashrah, and said Allah had cured him and that he disliked spreading evil among the people. Surah al-Falaq names the blowing on knots. The answer in his life was revelation and ruqyah, not more magic.

items.title: When the whisper comes
items.arabic:
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ
items.transliteration: A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. Rabbi a'udhu bika min hamazatish-shayatin wa a'udhu bika Rabbi an yahdurun. Amantu billah.
items.meaning: I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast shaytan. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the prodding of the devils, and I seek refuge in You from their being present. I believe in Allah.
items.when: When a filthy thought about Allah, the Prophet ﷺ, or wudu and prayer will not leave. Seek refuge, stop arguing with the thought, and carry on with the worship. If the thoughts are despair, panic, or a wish to harm yourself, treat that as health as well and speak to a clinician. The worship remains, and it is not the whole of the care.
items.virtue: The Companions said they found thoughts so heavy they would rather fall from the sky than speak them. He said that is the sign of faith, plain and clear, and told them to say: I believe in Allah. Shaytan cannot force a thought into a deed.

items.title: Honey, a healing named in the Qur'an
items.arabic: يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ
items.transliteration: Yakhruju min butuniha sharabun mukhtalifun alwanuhu fihi shifa'un lin-nas.
items.meaning: There comes from their bellies a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for people.
items.when: Honey is food and a prophetic medicine. A man whose brother had diarrhea was told to give him honey, and told again when the man thought it had made the illness worse, until the brother recovered. Use it as food. Do not stop a prescribed treatment because of a spoon of honey, and do not give honey to an infant under one year.
items.virtue: The Qur'an calls it a healing. The hadith shows him using it as a means, and still insisting the means be given its chance.

items.title: Black seed
items.arabic: فِي الْحَبَّةِ السَّوْدَاءِ شِفَاءٌ مِنْ كُلِّ دَاءٍ إِلَّا السَّامَ
items.transliteration: Fil-habbatis-sawda'i shifa'un min kulli da'in illas-sam.
items.meaning: In the black seed there is healing from every disease except death.
items.when: It is a food the Prophet ﷺ named. Ibn Shihab said the exception, death, is poison, and others said it means every fatal end. Use it as food in ordinary amounts. It is not a dose chart, and it is not a reason to refuse medicine for cancer, infection, or any named disease.
items.virtue: A true report about a created means. The Healer is still Allah.

items.title: Cupping, done by someone trained
items.arabic: إِنْ كَانَ فِي شَيْءٍ مِمَّا تَدَاوَوْنَ بِهِ خَيْرٌ فَالْحِجَامَةُ
items.transliteration: In kana fi shay'in mimma tadawawna bihi khayrun fal-hijamah.
items.meaning: If there is good in any of the treatments you use, then it is in cupping.
items.when: He ﷺ was treated with hijama and recommended it. If you use it, go to a person trained to do it cleanly. This page does not teach the cutting. Infection, blood thinners, pregnancy, and anemia are reasons to ask a clinician first.
items.virtue: A sunnah means of treatment, in the same family as seeking a cure, not a spiritual secret.

items.title: Do not go to a fortune-teller
items.arabic: مَنْ أَتَى عَرَّافًا فَسَأَلَهُ عَنْ شَيْءٍ لَمْ تُقْبَلْ لَهُ صَلَاةٌ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً
items.transliteration: Man ata arrafan fa-sa'alahu an shay'in lam tuqbal lahu salatun arba'ina laylah.
items.meaning: Whoever goes to a fortune-teller and asks him about something, his prayer is not accepted for forty nights.
items.when: This is the boundary of Ruhani Ilaj. A person who claims to know the unseen, to speak with your name through jinn, or to read your future is not a healer. Asking them, even once, is the harm in this hadith. Believing them is worse: a report in the Sunan says whoever goes to a soothsayer and believes him has disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ.
items.virtue: The forty nights are a warning, not a curiosity. Stay with Qur'an, dua, and a doctor.
items.reference: Sahih Muslim 2230. Believing the soothsayer: Sunan Abi Dawud 3904

items.title: Do not hang a talisman
items.arabic: مَنْ عَلَّقَ تَمِيمَةً فَقَدْ أَشْرَكَ
items.transliteration: Man allaqa tamimatan fa-qad ashrak.
items.meaning: Whoever hangs an amulet has committed shirk.
items.when: Do not wear or hang number squares, unknown letters, strings, or a ta'weez bought as a guarantee. Recite instead. Scholars differed about a case that contains only Qur'an, with nothing else. The safer path, and the one free of that disagreement, is not to hang it. The Prophet's ﷺ practice was recitation, blowing, and dua, not a pendant.
items.virtue: Ruqyah is open and spoken. A locked amulet hides what the heart is trusting.
items.reference: Musnad Ahmad, from Uqbah ibn Amir. Graded sahih by later hadith scholars for this wording. The safer practice is agreed: recite, do not depend on a charm.
items.note: The sahih replacement is the ruqyah of the hand on the pain, Sahih Muslim 2202, earlier in this section.

items.title: Do not call on the jinn
items.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمْ رَهَقًا
items.transliteration: Wa annahu kana rijalun minal-insi ya'udhuna bi-rijalin minal-jinni fa-zaduhum rahaqa.
items.meaning: And there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, and they only increased them in distress.
items.when: If a website, a pir, or a healer tells you to call a jinn, name a star, write a square, or slaughter for someone other than Allah, refuse. Seeking refuge is in Allah and in His words. That is the whole of this section.
items.virtue: The Qur'an says seeking refuge in the jinn increased their burden. Ruqyah goes the other way.

items.title: Water over which the Qur'an is recited
items.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
ثُمَّ آيَةُ الْكُرْسِيِّ وَالْمُعَوِّذَاتُ، ثُمَّ النَّفْثُ الْيَسِيرُ
items.transliteration: The established act is recitation and a light breath, as he ﷺ blew after the Mu'awwidhat. Drinking water afterward is a widespread practice built on that, not a separate hadith with a recipe.
items.meaning: Recite, blow lightly into the hands or toward the water, and drink or wipe. Do not add saffron squares, unknown names, or a claimed secret count.
items.when: For yourself or your family, after the recitation on this page. Zamzam may be drunk with a sincere dua. The report 'Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for' is in Sunan Ibn Majah 3062, and scholars differed on its chain, so it is not listed here as sahih.
items.virtue: The firm sunnah is the recitation and the breath. Keep the extra step humble, and do not let it become the product.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 5735 for blowing after the Mu'awwidhat. Zamzam: Sunan Ibn Majah 3062, disputed
items.note: No measurement, no ink, and no written charm belongs in the water.

items.title: Good in this world and the next
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
items.transliteration: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah wa fil-akhirati hasanah wa qina adhaban-nar.
items.meaning: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the next world, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
items.when: The Prophet ﷺ made this dua often. It is also the dua between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone during tawaf.
items.virtue: Allah quotes it as the dua of the people who ask for both lives, not for this world alone.
items.reference: Qur'an 2:201. Its frequent use is in Sahih al-Bukhari 4522 and Sahih Muslim 2690.

items.title: The closing dua of al-Baqarah
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ ۖ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا ۚ أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
items.transliteration: Rabbana la tu'akhidhna in nasina aw akhta'na. Rabbana wa la tahmil alayna isran kama hamaltahu alalladhina min qablina. Rabbana wa la tuhammilna ma la taqata lana bih. Wa'fu anna waghfir lana warhamna. Anta mawlana fansurna alal-qawmil-kafirin.
items.meaning: Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or fall into error. Our Lord, do not lay on us a burden like the one You laid on those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with more than we can bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against the people who reject the truth.
items.when: In any dua, and with the two closing verses of al-Baqarah at night. The full two verses are in Azkar.
items.virtue: Allah said: I have answered. That is in the hadith of the two verses, Sahih Muslim 125 and 126.

items.title: Do not let our hearts swerve
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ
items.transliteration: Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana wa hab lana min ladunka rahmah. Innaka antal-Wahhab.
items.meaning: Our Lord, do not turn our hearts away after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. You are the Giver.
items.when: When you fear a change in the heart, and as a daily dua for steadfastness.
items.virtue: It is the dua of those firmly grounded in knowledge, after they hear the unclear verses and say: we believe in all of it.

items.title: We have believed, so forgive us
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
items.transliteration: Rabbana innana amanna faghfir lana dhunubana wa qina adhaban-nar.
items.meaning: Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
items.when: Any sitting of dua.
items.virtue: Allah quotes it among the words of the patient, the truthful, the devout, and those who ask forgiveness before dawn.

items.title: Forgive our sins and our excess
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِي أَمْرِنَا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
items.transliteration: Rabbanaghfir lana dhunubana wa israfana fi amrina wa thabbit aqdamana wansurna alal-qawmil-kafirin.
items.meaning: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affairs, make our feet firm, and give us victory over the people who reject the truth.
items.when: When asking for firmness after a mistake.
items.virtue: The Qur'an says Allah gave them the reward of this world and the best reward of the next, for this dua was their answer under hardship.

items.title: We heard a caller to faith
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي لِلْإِيمَانِ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ فَآمَنَّا ۚ رَبَّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَكَفِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّئَاتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ الْأَبْرَارِ ۝ رَبَّنَا وَآتِنَا مَا وَعَدْتَّنَا عَلَى رُسُلِكَ وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ۗ إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ
items.transliteration: Rabbana innana sami'na munadiyan yunadi lil-imani an aminu bi rabbikum fa'amanna. Rabbana faghfir lana dhunubana wa kaffir anna sayyi'atina wa tawaffana ma'al-abrar. Rabbana wa atina ma wa'adtana ala rusulika wa la tukhzina yawmal-qiyamah. Innaka la tukhliful-mi'ad.
items.meaning: Our Lord, we heard a caller calling to faith, 'Believe in your Lord,' and we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, blot out our bad deeds, and take us in death with the righteous. Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. You do not break Your promise.
items.when: A long personal dua, especially at night. It follows the verses about people who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides.
items.virtue: Allah says their Lord answers them: I do not let the work of any worker among you go to waste.

items.title: Accept from us
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ۝ رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنَا أُمَّةً مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
items.transliteration: Rabbana taqabbal minna innaka antas-Sami'ul-Alim. Rabbana waj'alna muslimayni laka wa min dhurriyyatina ummatan muslimatan laka wa arina manasikana wa tub alayna innaka antat-Tawwabur-Rahim.
items.meaning: Our Lord, accept this from us. You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, make us both submitted to You, and from our descendants a community submitted to You. Show us our rites, and turn to us. You are the One who accepts repentance, the Merciful.
items.when: After building any good work, as Ibrahim and Isma'il said while raising the foundations of the House.
items.virtue: It joins acceptance, offspring who remain Muslim, and repentance.

items.title: Ibrahim's dua for prayer and for parents
items.arabic: رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ ۝ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسَابُ
items.transliteration: Rabbij'alni muqimas-salati wa min dhurriyyati. Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a'. Rabbanaghfir li wa liwalidayya wa lil-mu'minina yawma yaqumul-hisab.
items.meaning: My Lord, make me steadfast in the prayer, and from my descendants as well. Our Lord, accept my dua. Our Lord, forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day the account is established.
items.when: For your own salah, your children, your parents, and the believers.
items.virtue: A complete dua of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: worship, offspring, acceptance, and forgiveness.

items.title: Mercy for parents
items.arabic: رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا
items.transliteration: Rabbir-hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira.
items.meaning: My Lord, have mercy on them both as they raised me when I was small.
items.when: For parents who are alive or who died upon faith. The verse sits inside the command to lower the wing of humility to them and to speak to them with noble words. If a parent died outside Islam, ask a scholar before using a funeral-style dua; the Prophet's ﷺ guidance about his own parents is a separate, sensitive question.
items.virtue: It is the Qur'an's own dua of gratitude for upbringing.

items.title: Nuh's dua for parents and the believers
items.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًا
items.transliteration: Rabbighfir li wa liwalidayya wa liman dakhala baytiya mu'minan wa lil-mu'minina wal-mu'minat, wa la tazididh-dhalimina illa tabara.
items.meaning: My Lord, forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin.
items.when: For the household and for the whole community of believers.
items.virtue: The closing dua of Surah Nuh.

items.title: A true entering and a true leaving
items.arabic: رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَاجْعَلْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ سُلْطَانًا نَصِيرًا
items.transliteration: Rabbi adkhilni mudkhala sidqin wa akhrijni mukhraja sidqin waj'al li min ladunka sultanan nasira.
items.meaning: My Lord, cause me to enter a true entrance and to leave a true leaving, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.
items.when: Before a new home, a journey, a responsibility, or any beginning and ending you want to be honest.
items.virtue: Revealed as a dua of the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah, and it remains a dua for every truthful passage.

items.title: Musa's dua for an open chest
items.arabic: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي
items.transliteration: Rabbish-rah li sadri wa yassir li amri wahlul uqdatan min lisani yafqahu qawli.
items.meaning: My Lord, open my chest, make my task easy, and undo the knot from my tongue so they understand my speech.
items.when: Before speaking, teaching, an exam, or any hard task. Musa, peace be upon him, asked it before going to Pharaoh.
items.virtue: Allah answered him and reminded him of His earlier favors.

items.title: Increase me in knowledge
items.arabic: رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
items.transliteration: Rabbi zidni ilma.
items.meaning: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
items.when: Before study, after study, and whenever you open a book. The verse tells the Prophet ﷺ not to rush the revelation, then gives him this dua.
items.virtue: It is the Qur'an's short dua for knowledge. Useful knowledge is the kind that makes you more obedient.

items.title: The dua of Yunus
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minadh-dhalimin.
items.meaning: There is no god except You. Glory be to You. I have been among the wrongdoers.
items.when: In any distress: fear, illness, debt, or a sin you regret. Say it with the meaning, not as a spell.
items.virtue: No Muslim calls upon Allah with it for anything except that Allah answers him. That report is in Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3505, and the words themselves are Qur'an 21:87. Allah says: We responded to him and saved him from the grief, and thus do We save the believers.

items.title: Refuge from the prodding of the devils
items.arabic: رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
items.transliteration: Rabbi a'udhu bika min hamazatish-shayatini wa a'udhu bika Rabbi an yahdurun.
items.meaning: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the prodding of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their being present with me.
items.when: When a whisper, a temptation, or a fear of the shaytan comes. Also in Ruhani Ilaj under protection.
items.virtue: It is a Qur'anic ruqyah against waswas. Pair it with a'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim.

items.title: Forgive and have mercy
items.arabic: رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
items.transliteration: Rabbighfir warham wa Anta khayrur-rahimin.
items.meaning: My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of those who show mercy.
items.when: A short closing for any dua.
items.virtue: The last verse of Surah al-Mu'minun.

items.title: Coolness of the eyes in the family
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
items.transliteration: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina wa dhurriyyatina qurrata a'yunin waj'alna lil-muttaqina imama.
items.meaning: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our children comfort to our eyes, and make us an example for the people of taqwa.
items.when: For a marriage and for children. The comfort asked for is faith and good character, not appearance or wealth.
items.virtue: It is the dua of the servants of the Most Merciful in Surah al-Furqan.

items.title: Ibrahim asks for sound judgment
items.arabic: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ وَاجْعَلْ لِي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ
items.transliteration: Rabbi hab li hukman wa alhiqni bissalihin. Waj'al li lisana sidqin fil-akhirin. Waj'alni min warathati jannatin-na'im.
items.meaning: My Lord, grant me sound judgment and join me with the righteous. Give me a true reputation among later people. Make me one of the heirs of the Garden of bliss.
items.when: When you want your work to outlive you in a true way, not as fame.
items.virtue: Ibrahim's dua, and Allah calls this a reminder and a praise left behind.

items.title: No grudge toward the believers
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَانِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ
items.transliteration: Rabbanaghfir lana wa li-ikhwaninalladhina sabaquna bil-imani wa la taj'al fi qulubina ghillan lilladhina amanu. Rabbana innaka Ra'ufun Rahim.
items.meaning: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who went ahead of us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any grudge toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are Kind, Merciful.
items.when: After a quarrel, and as a dua for the earlier generations of believers.
items.virtue: The Qur'an places it on the tongues of those who come after the Muhajirun and the Ansar.

items.title: Complete our light
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
items.transliteration: Rabbana atmim lana nurana waghfir lana innaka ala kulli shay'in Qadir.
items.meaning: Our Lord, complete for us our light and forgive us. You are able to do all things.
items.when: On the Last Day the hypocrites will ask the believers for some of their light. This is the believers' dua then, and it is a dua now for a faith that lasts.
items.virtue: Qur'an 66:8, the day Allah will not disgrace the Prophet ﷺ and those who believed with him.

items.title: The young men of the cave
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
items.transliteration: Rabbana atina min ladunka rahmatan wa hayyi' lana min amrina rashada.
items.meaning: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself, and arrange for us, in our affair, right guidance.
items.when: When you take a difficult, lonely, or unpopular stand for the sake of faith.
items.virtue: The youths of the cave said it, and Allah spread His mercy over them and prepared them.

items.title: Zakariyya's dua for a good child
items.arabic: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ
items.transliteration: Rabbi hab li min ladunka dhurriyyatan tayyibah. Innaka Sami'ud-du'a'.
items.meaning: My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. You are the Hearer of dua.
items.when: For a child, and for the child to be good. Zakariyya, peace be upon him, asked it in old age, quietly.
items.virtue: Allah gave him the good news of Yahya.

items.title: Pour patience on us
items.arabic: رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
items.transliteration: Rabbana afrigh alayna sabran wa thabbit aqdamana wansurna alal-qawmil-kafirin.
items.meaning: Our Lord, pour patience upon us, make our feet firm, and give us victory over the people who reject the truth.
items.when: When a trial is larger than your strength. Talut's people said it facing Jalut.
items.virtue: Allah says they defeated them by Allah's permission.

items.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar, the chief plea for forgiveness
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
items.transliteration: Allahumma Anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa Ant. Khalaqtani wa ana abduk, wa ana ala ahdika wa wa'dika mastata't. A'udhu bika min sharri ma sana't. Abu'u laka bini'matika alayya wa abu'u bidhanbi. Faghfir li, fa-innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Ant.
items.meaning: O Allah, You are my Lord. There is no god except You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I am holding to Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I admit to You Your favor upon me, and I admit my sin. Forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.
items.when: Morning, and again in the evening. It is also listed among the morning and evening azkar.
items.virtue: Whoever says it with certainty in the morning and dies that day enters Paradise. Whoever says it with certainty at night and dies that night enters Paradise.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6306, from Shaddad ibn Aws

items.title: I have wronged myself greatly
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي ظُلْمًا كَثِيرًا، وَلَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَغْفِرَةً مِنْ عِنْدِكَ وَارْحَمْنِي، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
items.transliteration: Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran, wa la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Ant, faghfir li maghfiratan min indika warhamni, innaka Antal-Ghafurur-Rahim.
items.meaning: O Allah, I have wronged myself with a great wrong, and no one forgives sins except You, so forgive me with forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.
items.when: Before the salam, at the end of the prayer. Abu Bakr asked for a dua to say in his salah, and this is what he was taught. Some narrations say kathiran wa kabira.
items.virtue: A dua the Prophet ﷺ chose for the closest of his Companions.

items.title: Refuge from worry, debt, and helplessness
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ غَلَبَةِ الدَّيْنِ وَقَهْرِ الرِّجَالِ
items.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan, wa a'udhu bika minal-ajzi wal-kasal, wa a'udhu bika minal-jubni wal-bukhl, wa a'udhu bika min ghalabatid-dayni wa qahrir-rijal.
items.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from inability and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, and from being overcome by debt and overpowered by men.
items.when: When anxiety, sadness, debt, or fear of people sits on the chest. He ﷺ used to seek refuge with these words often.
items.virtue: Anas said: I would repeat them.

items.title: The words for grief and heavy debt
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illallahul-Azimul-Halim. La ilaha illallahu Rabbul-arshil-azim. La ilaha illallahu Rabbussamawati wa Rabbul-ardi wa Rabbul-arshil-karim.
items.meaning: There is no god except Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god except Allah, Lord of the magnificent Throne. There is no god except Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the noble Throne.
items.when: When grief or a heavy debt closes in. Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ used to say this at the time of grief.
items.virtue: These are words of tawhid, not a charm. The relief, if it comes, comes from Allah.

items.title: I hope for Your mercy
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَحْمَتَكَ أَرْجُو، فَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
items.transliteration: Allahumma rahmataka arju, fa-la takilni ila nafsi tarfata ayn, wa aslih li sha'ni kullahu, la ilaha illa Ant.
items.meaning: O Allah, it is Your mercy I hope for, so do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, and set right for me all of my affair. There is no god except You.
items.when: In the morning and the evening, and whenever you feel unable to carry your own affair.
items.virtue: Abu Bakrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said these words are a supplication of distress.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5090, from Abu Bakrah

items.title: Keep my heart firm on Your religion
items.arabic: يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ
items.transliteration: Ya Muqallibal-qulub, thabbit qalbi ala dinik.
items.meaning: O Turner of the hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion.
items.when: Often. He ﷺ used to swear that the heart is between two fingers of the Most Merciful, and that He turns it as He wills. Asked why he made this dua so much, he said the heart is between the fingers of Allah.
items.virtue: A dua for steadfastness, from the one who was already the most steadfast.

items.title: You love to pardon, so pardon me
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
items.transliteration: Allahumma innaka Afuwwun tuhibbul-afwa fa'fu anni.
items.meaning: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.
items.when: Aishah asked what to say if she reached Laylat al-Qadr. He told her this. It is also a beautiful dua on any night of Ramadan, and outside it.
items.virtue: The dua he chose for the night that is better than a thousand months.

items.title: Istikhara, asking Allah to choose
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي، فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ. وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي، فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ، ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ
items.transliteration: Allahumma inni astakhiruka bi-ilmik, wa astaqdiruka bi-qudratik, wa as'aluka min fadlikal-azim, fa-innaka taqdiru wa la aqdir, wa ta'lamu wa la a'lam, wa Anta Allamul-ghuyub. Allahumma in kunta ta'lamu anna hadhal-amra khayrun li fi dini wa ma'ashi wa aqibati amri, faqdurhu li wa yassirhu li thumma barik li fih. Wa in kunta ta'lamu anna hadhal-amra sharrun li fi dini wa ma'ashi wa aqibati amri, fasrifhu anni wasrifni anh, waqdur liyal-khayra haythu kan, thumma ardini bih.
items.meaning: O Allah, I ask You to choose for me by Your knowledge, and I ask You to decree for me by Your power, and I ask You from Your immense favor. You are able and I am not. You know and I do not. You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair, then decree it for me, make it easy, and bless me in it. And if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, decree good for me wherever it is, and make me content with it.
items.when: For a decision that is allowed, not for something already haram or already a clear duty. Pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer, then say this and name the matter in place of 'this matter.' Jabir said he used to teach them istikhara as he taught them a surah of the Qur'an.
items.virtue: The answer is not a required dream. Go ahead with what is facilitated and what keeps your religion safe, and be content with Allah's choice. A dream can be a mercy, and it is not a condition.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6382, from Jabir ibn Abdullah
items.note: Istikhara is dua after two rak'ahs. It is not opening a book at random, and it is not asking a fortune-teller.

items.title: Qunut in Witr
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي فِيمَنْ هَدَيْتَ، وَعَافِنِي فِيمَنْ عَافَيْتَ، وَتَوَلَّنِي فِيمَنْ تَوَلَّيْتَ، وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، وَقِنِي شَرَّ مَا قَضَيْتَ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْضِي وَلَا يُقْضَى عَلَيْكَ، وَإِنَّهُ لَا يَذِلُّ مَنْ وَالَيْتَ، وَلَا يَعِزُّ مَنْ عَادَيْتَ، تَبَارَكْتَ رَبَّنَا وَتَعَالَيْتَ
items.transliteration: Allahummahdini fiman hadayt, wa afini fiman afayt, wa tawallani fiman tawallayt, wa barik li fima a'tayt, wa qini sharra ma qadayt, fa-innaka taqdi wa la yuqda alayk, wa innahu la yadhillu man walayt, wa la ya'izzu man adayt. Tabarakta Rabbana wa ta'alayt.
items.meaning: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me wellbeing among those You have granted wellbeing, take me into Your care among those You have taken into Your care, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. You decree and nothing is decreed over You. Whoever You take as a friend is not humiliated, and whoever You take as an enemy is not honored. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted.
items.when: In the qunut of Witr, as al-Hasan ibn Ali reported. Schools differ on raising the hands, saying it before or after ruku, and whether a person adds salawat. Follow the imam and the school you pray with.
items.virtue: At-Tirmidhi graded the hadith of al-Hasan hasan, and he said nothing is known from the Prophet ﷺ about qunut in Witr better than this.

items.title: After wudu
items.arabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ. اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي مِنَ التَّوَّابِينَ وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنَ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
items.transliteration: Ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluh. Allahummaj'alni minat-tawwabina waj'alni minal-mutatahhirin.
items.meaning: I bear witness that there is no god except Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. O Allah, make me among those who constantly repent and among those who purify themselves.
items.when: After finishing wudu. The shahadah is in Sahih Muslim. The second sentence is in at-Tirmidhi.
items.virtue: Whoever says the shahadah after wudu, the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him and he may enter by whichever he wishes.
items.reference: Sahih Muslim 234; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 55 for the second sentence

items.title: Entering the mosque
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
items.transliteration: Allahummaftah li abwaba rahmatik.
items.meaning: O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.
items.when: Enter with the right foot, send salawat, and say this. A fuller form in Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also asks refuge from the outcast shaytan.
items.virtue: The mosque is entered asking for mercy.

items.title: Leaving the mosque
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
items.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik.
items.meaning: O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.
items.when: Leave with the left foot. Mercy was asked on the way in. Bounty, including lawful provision, is asked on the way out.
items.virtue: The pair is in Sahih Muslim from Abu Humayd or Abu Usayd.

items.title: Before entering the toilet
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبُثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ
items.transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith.
items.meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female devils.
items.when: Before stepping into the place where you relieve yourself. Say it outside, then enter with the left foot.
items.virtue: He ﷺ said this before entering the privy.

items.title: After leaving the toilet
items.arabic: غُفْرَانَكَ
items.transliteration: Ghufranak.
items.meaning: I ask Your forgiveness.
items.when: Just after leaving. A short dua of Aishah's report: the Prophet ﷺ used to say it when he came out.
items.virtue: At-Tirmidhi graded it hasan, and it is the sunnah wording in the books of adhkar.

items.title: Before eating
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
items.transliteration: Bismillah.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah.
items.when: Before the first bite. If you forget and then remember, say the next dua. He told Umar ibn Abi Salamah: say the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.
items.virtue: Shaytan is kept from sharing a meal that begins with the name of Allah. That meaning is in Sahih Muslim 2017.

items.title: If you forgot the name at the start of the meal
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ
items.transliteration: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah at its beginning and at its end.
items.when: As soon as you remember during the meal.
items.virtue: The Prophet ﷺ said: if one of you eats and forgets to mention Allah, let him say this.

items.title: After eating
items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
items.transliteration: Alhamdu lillahilladhi at'amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah.
items.meaning: Praise belongs to Allah, who fed me this and provided it for me without any power or strength from me.
items.when: After the meal. Another sahih praise, when the dish is lifted, is: Alhamdu lillahi hamdan kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fih.
items.virtue: His past sins are forgiven. That is the report in the Sunan for this wording. The many-praises wording pleased Allah so much that several angels raced to write it, in Sahih al-Bukhari 5458.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 4023; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3458. The second praise: Sahih al-Bukhari 5458

items.title: Entering the home
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا، وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا، وَعَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا
items.transliteration: Bismillahi walajna, wa bismillahi kharajna, wa alallahi Rabbina tawakkalna.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon Allah, our Lord, we rely.
items.when: As you enter the house. Give salam to the people inside, and if the house is empty still say salam, for Allah says: give a greeting that is better or return it.
items.virtue: Say it, and then tell the shaytan: there is no lodging for you here tonight.

items.title: Leaving the home
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
items.transliteration: Bismillah, tawakkaltu alallah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah.
items.when: As you step out of the house.
items.virtue: It is said to you: you have been guided, defended, and protected, and the devil goes far from you. At-Tirmidhi called the hadith hasan sahih.

items.title: The longer dua when leaving
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَضِلَّ أَوْ أُضَلَّ، أَوْ أَزِلَّ أَوْ أُزَلَّ، أَوْ أَظْلِمَ أَوْ أُظْلَمَ، أَوْ أَجْهَلَ أَوْ يُجْهَلَ عَلَيَّ
items.transliteration: Bismillah, tawakkaltu alallah. Allahumma inni a'udhu bika an adilla aw udall, aw azilla aw uzall, aw azlima aw uzlam, aw ajhala aw yujhala alayy.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from going astray or being led astray, from slipping or being made to slip, from wronging or being wronged, from acting ignorantly or having ignorance acted upon me.
items.when: When the Prophet ﷺ left his house, as Umm Salamah reported. Some routes say 'be humiliated or be made humiliated' in place of 'slip.' The ask is the same: protection on the way out.
items.virtue: At-Tirmidhi graded a form of it hasan sahih. Riyad as-Salihin records it as number 82.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5094; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3427; Riyad as-Salihin 82

items.title: When you wear a new garment
items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي كَسَانِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
items.transliteration: Alhamdu lillahilladhi kasani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah.
items.meaning: Praise belongs to Allah, who clothed me with this and provided it for me without any power or strength from me.
items.when: When you put on something new. He also used to name the garment and say, for example, praise belongs to Allah who clothed me with this.
items.virtue: Allah forgives his past sins.

items.title: When someone sneezes
items.arabic:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ
يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَكُمْ
items.transliteration: The one who sneezes: Alhamdu lillah. The listener: Yarhamukallah. The reply: Yahdikumullahu wa yuslihu balakum.
items.meaning: Praise belongs to Allah. May Allah have mercy on you. May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.
items.when: Only if the person praised Allah. If they do not say alhamdulillah, you do not owe the reply. If they sneeze again and again, reply the first times and then make dua for their recovery in your own words. Coaches differ on the exact count after three; the certain sunnah is to answer the one who praises Allah.
items.virtue: It is a right of a Muslim upon a Muslim, in Sahih al-Bukhari 6224 and Sahih Muslim 2162.

items.title: When anger rises
items.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
items.transliteration: A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim.
items.meaning: I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast shaytan.
items.when: As soon as you feel anger. If you are standing, sit. If you are sitting, lie down. Stay quiet rather than deciding in that state. Two men insulted each other in his presence and he said: I know a word which, if he said it, what he finds would leave him.
items.virtue: Anger is a door the shaytan uses. The refuge is said to Allah, not to a charm.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6115; Sahih Muslim 2610. Sitting and lying: Sunan Abi Dawud 4782

items.title: The dua of travel
items.arabic: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ
items.transliteration: Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun. Allahumma inna nas'aluka fi safarina hadhal-birra wat-taqwa, wa minal-amali ma tarda. Allahumma hawwin alayna safarana hadha watwi anna bu'dah. Allahumma Antas-sahibu fis-safari wal-khalifatu fil-ahl. Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min wa'tha'is-safari wa ka'abatil-manzari wa su'il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahl.
items.meaning: Allah is greatest, three times. Glory be to the One who subjected this for us, and we could not have subdued it, and to our Lord we will surely return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey for righteousness and taqwa, and for deeds You are pleased with. O Allah, make this journey easy for us and fold up its distance. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Guardian over the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a gloomy sight, and from a bad return in wealth and family.
items.when: When you settle onto the mount, into the car, or onto the journey. On the way home, add the return phrase in the next card. The first glorification is also Qur'an 43:13-14.
items.virtue: Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this whenever he mounted his camel for a journey.

items.title: When returning from a journey
items.arabic: آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
items.transliteration: Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun.
items.meaning: We are returning, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord.
items.when: Add it to the travel dua on the way home. He also used to say Allahu Akbar three times when he saw the walls of Madinah, then this phrase.
items.virtue: Sahih Muslim 1342 includes it in the return. The arrival at Madinah is in Sahih al-Bukhari 1797 and Sahih Muslim 1345.

items.title: When rain falls
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَيِّبًا نَافِعًا
items.transliteration: Allahumma sayyiban nafi'a.
items.meaning: O Allah, make it a beneficial downpour.
items.when: When you see the rain. Aishah said he would say this. If the rain is harmful, the established dua is to ask that it fall around you, not on the homes: Allahumma hawalayna wa la alayna.
items.virtue: Rain is a mercy. The dua asks that it stay beneficial.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 1032. For a harmful storm: Sahih al-Bukhari 1014

items.title: Asking Allah for rain
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا، اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا، اللَّهُمَّ أَغِثْنَا
items.transliteration: Allahumma aghithna, Allahumma aghithna, Allahumma aghithna.
items.meaning: O Allah, give us rain. Three times.
items.when: In a drought. A man asked during the Friday sermon, and the Prophet ﷺ made this dua. Clouds came before they left the mosque. The full salat al-istisqa has a known form in the fiqh books. This is the dua itself.
items.virtue: Anas reported the rain continuing until the next Friday, when they asked for it to be lifted.

items.title: When you hear thunder
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي يُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ
items.transliteration: Subhanalladhi yusabbihur-ra'du bihamdihi wal-mala'ikatu min khifatih.
items.meaning: Glory be to the One whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and so do the angels, out of fear of Him.
items.when: When thunder is heard. Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr would stop speaking and say this. It is a Companion's practice, and the words are built from Qur'an 13:13.
items.virtue: Imam Malik recorded it in al-Muwatta. It is not a hadith traced with a full chain to the Prophet ﷺ in that book, so the grade here is Reported.
items.reference: Muwatta Malik, the report of Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr; Qur'an 13:13

items.title: Enough of what is lawful
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
items.transliteration: Allahummakfini bihalalika an haramik, wa aghnini bifadlik amman siwak.
items.meaning: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your favor so I need no one besides You.
items.when: For debt, poverty, and the fear of falling into the haram to cover a need. Ali taught it to a man in debt, as a servant who had been bound reported.
items.virtue: At-Tirmidhi graded it hasan. It asks for halal sufficiency. It is not a promise that a number of recitations will cancel a contract.

items.title: When breaking the fast
items.arabic: ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَثَبَتَ الْأَجْرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
items.transliteration: Dhahabadh-dhama'u wabtallatil-uruqu wa thabatal-ajru in sha Allah.
items.meaning: The thirst has gone, the veins are quenched, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.
items.when: At iftar. The fasting person's dua is a time of hope, so ask in these words or in your own. Hadith scholars differed on the chain of this particular sentence. Wanting Allah at iftar does not depend on this one wording.
items.virtue: The Prophet ﷺ said the fasting person has a dua that is not turned back. That virtue is reported by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Use the moment. Do not treat one sentence as a mechanism.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 2357 for this wording. The virtue of the fasting person's dua: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3598
items.note: Grade is Reported because scholars differed on the chain. The act of making dua at iftar is the sound practice.

items.title: Dua in sujud
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا وَبِحَمْدِكَ، اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي
items.transliteration: Subhanaka Allahumma Rabbana wa bihamdik. Allahummaghfir li.
items.meaning: Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise belongs to You. O Allah, forgive me.
items.when: In sujud, after Subhana rabbiyal-a'la. Then ask for whatever you need, in Arabic or in your own language. The closest a servant is to his Lord is while he is in sujud, so increase dua there.
items.virtue: He ﷺ used to say the sentence above often in his ruku and sujud, as Aishah reported, reading the Qur'an's command to glorify and seek forgiveness.
