items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 817; Sahih Muslim 484. The closeness in sujud: Sahih Muslim 482

items.title: Ayat al-Kursi in the morning and the evening
items.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
items.transliteration: Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum. La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm. Lahu ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard. Man dhalladhi yashfa'u indahu illa bi-idhnih. Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum. Wa la yuhituna bi-shay'in min ilmihi illa bima sha'. Wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samawati wal-ard. Wa la ya'uduhu hifdhuhuma. Wa Huwal-Aliyyul-Azim.
items.meaning: Allah, there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and guarding them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
items.when: Once in the morning adhkar and once in the evening adhkar. The same verse is also read after each obligatory prayer and before sleep. Those two reports are firmer, and they have their own cards.
items.virtue: It is the greatest verse of the Qur'an, as the Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b, in Sahih Muslim 810. A report that whoever reads it in the morning is protected until evening is carried in the books of adhkar. Reciting it is Qur'an whether or not one is relying on that particular chain.
items.reference: Qur'an 2:255. The greatest verse: Sahih Muslim 810

items.title: Al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas, three times
items.arabic:
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ۝ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ۝ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ۝ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
items.transliteration:
Qul Huwallahu Ahad. Allahus-Samad. Lam yalid wa lam yulad. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad.

Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbil-falaq. Min sharri ma khalaq. Wa min sharri ghasqin idha waqab. Wa min sharrin-naffathati fil-uqad. Wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad.

Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbin-nas. Malikin-nas. Ilahin-nas. Min sharril-waswasil-khannas. Alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas. Minal-jinnati wan-nas.
items.meaning:
Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He does not beget and He was not begotten, and there is none equal to Him.

Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He created, from the evil of darkness when it settles, from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.

Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers in the chests of mankind, from among jinn and mankind.
items.when: Three times in the morning and three times in the evening. Abdullah ibn Khubaib said they asked him for words to say at those two times, and he told them to recite these three surahs three times.
items.virtue: They will be enough for you against everything. At-Tirmidhi graded the hadith hasan sahih.
items.reference: Qur'an 112, 113, and 114. Sunan Abi Dawud 5082; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3575

items.title: In the name of Allah, nothing harms alongside His name
items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
items.transliteration: Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru ma'asmihi shay'un fil-ardi wa la fis-sama'i wa Huwas-Sami'ul-Alim.
items.meaning: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can harm, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
items.when: Three times in the morning and three times in the evening.
items.virtue: Uthman ibn Affan reported: nothing will harm him. At-Tirmidhi graded it hasan sahih. Aban ibn Uthman once did not say it, was struck by a paralysis, and then told the people the hadith, looking at them as one who had learned the cost of leaving it.
items.reference: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3388; Sunan Abi Dawud 5088; Riyad as-Salihin 1457

items.title: I am pleased with Allah as Lord
items.arabic: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَبِيًّا
items.transliteration: Raditu billahi Rabba, wa bil-islami dina, wa bi-Muhammadin sallallahu alayhi wa sallam nabiyya.
items.meaning: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as prophet.
items.when: Three times in the morning and three times in the evening.
items.virtue: Whoever says it in the morning, it becomes a right upon Allah to please him on the Day of Resurrection. A related sahih report says whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as messenger has tasted the sweetness of faith.
items.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5072; Musnad Ahmad. The sweetness of faith: Sahih Muslim 34

items.title: We have entered the morning
items.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ. رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ. رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
items.transliteration: Asbahna wa asbahal-mulku lillah, walhamdu lillah, la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir. Rabbi as'aluka khayra ma fi hadhal-yawmi wa khayra ma ba'dah, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma fi hadhal-yawmi wa sharri ma ba'dah. Rabbi a'udhu bika minal-kasali wa su'il-kibar. Rabbi a'udhu bika min adhabin fin-nari wa adhabin fil-qabr.
items.meaning: We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah, and praise belongs to Allah. There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what comes after it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what comes after it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
items.when: In the morning. The evening uses the next card.
items.virtue: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said the Prophet ﷺ used to say this in the morning and the matching words in the evening.

items.title: We have entered the evening
items.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا. رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ. رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
items.transliteration: Amsayna wa amsal-mulku lillah, walhamdu lillah, la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir. Rabbi as'aluka khayra ma fi hadhihil-laylati wa khayra ma ba'daha, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma fi hadhihil-laylati wa sharri ma ba'daha. Rabbi a'udhu bika minal-kasali wa su'il-kibar. Rabbi a'udhu bika min adhabin fin-nari wa adhabin fil-qabr.
items.meaning: We have entered the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah, and praise belongs to Allah. There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what comes after it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what comes after it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
items.when: In the evening. It is the same hadith as the morning wording.
items.virtue: Sahih Muslim 2723.

items.title: By You we enter the morning
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
items.transliteration: Allahumma bika asbahna, wa bika amsayna, wa bika nahya, wa bika namut, wa ilaykan-nushur.
items.meaning: O Allah, by You we enter the morning, by You we enter the evening, by You we live, by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
items.when: In the morning.
items.virtue: Abu Hurayrah reported it as the Prophet's ﷺ morning wording.

items.title: By You we enter the evening
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ
items.transliteration: Allahumma bika amsayna, wa bika asbahna, wa bika nahya, wa bika namut, wa ilaykal-masir.
items.meaning: O Allah, by You we enter the evening, by You we enter the morning, by You we live, by You we die, and to You is the return.
items.when: In the evening. The closing word changes from resurrection to return.
items.virtue: The evening half of the same teaching.

items.title: Every blessing this morning is from You
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَصْبَحَ بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ أَوْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
items.transliteration: Allahumma ma asbaha bi min ni'matin aw bi-ahadin min khalqika fa-minka wahdaka la sharika lak, fa-lakal-hamdu wa lakash-shukr.
items.meaning: O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, or to any of Your creation, is from You alone, with no partner. So to You belongs the praise and to You belongs the thanks.
items.when: Once in the morning. The evening card changes asbaha to amsa.
items.virtue: Whoever says it in the morning has fulfilled the gratitude of that day, and whoever says the evening form has fulfilled the gratitude of that night.

items.title: Every blessing this evening is from You
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَمْسَى بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ أَوْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
items.transliteration: Allahumma ma amsa bi min ni'matin aw bi-ahadin min khalqika fa-minka wahdaka la sharika lak, fa-lakal-hamdu wa lakash-shukr.
items.meaning: O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me this evening, or to any of Your creation, is from You alone, with no partner. So to You belongs the praise and to You belongs the thanks.
items.when: Once in the evening.
items.virtue: It fulfills the gratitude of that night, in the report of Abdullah ibn Ghannam.

items.title: Allah is enough for me
items.arabic: حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ
items.transliteration: Hasbiyallahu la ilaha illa Huwa, alayhi tawakkaltu, wa Huwa Rabbul-arshil-azim.
items.meaning: Allah is enough for me. There is no god except Him. On Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the magnificent Throne.
items.when: Seven times in the morning and seven times in the evening.
items.virtue: Abu Dawud reports that Allah will suffice him in what worries him, of this world and the next. Some hadith scholars weakened the chain and some accepted it. The words themselves are the close of Surah at-Tawbah, so saying them is Qur'an.
items.note: The grade is Reported because the chain of the seven-times virtue was discussed. The verse is Qur'an.

items.title: Ten times after Fajr
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu, yuhyi wa yumit, wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir.
items.meaning: There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise. He gives life and gives death, and He is able to do all things.
items.when: Ten times after the Fajr prayer, before speaking if you can. The same ten times are said after Maghrib. That card is in the evening list.
items.virtue: Allah writes ten good deeds for him, erases ten sins, raises him ten degrees, and he has the like of freeing four slaves from the children of Isma'il. It is a protection from shaytan until the evening.

items.title: Ten times after Maghrib
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu, yuhyi wa yumit, wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir.
items.meaning: There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise. He gives life and gives death, and He is able to do all things.
items.when: Ten times after the Maghrib prayer.
items.virtue: The evening match of the Fajr remembrance, in the same family of reports.

items.title: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah
items.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
items.transliteration: A'udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq.
items.meaning: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created.
items.when: Three times in the evening. Also three times whenever you stop at a place on a journey, and nothing will harm you until you depart.
items.virtue: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ after being stung and said he had not said these words. The Prophet ﷺ told him that had he said them, nothing would have harmed him. Khawlah bint Hakim reported the wording for stopping at a place.

items.title: The last two verses of al-Baqarah
items.arabic:
آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۚ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ ۚ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ

لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ ۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ ۖ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا ۚ أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
items.transliteration:
Amanar-Rasulu bima unzila ilayhi mir-Rabbihi wal-mu'minun. Kullun amana billahi wa mala'ikatihi wa kutubihi wa rusulih. La nufarriqu bayna ahadin mir-rusulih. Wa qalu sami'na wa ata'na, ghufranaka Rabbana wa ilaykal-masir.

La yukallifullahu nafsan illa wus'aha. Laha ma kasabat wa alayha maktasabat. Rabbana la tu'akhidhna in nasina aw akhta'na. Rabbana wa la tahmil alayna isran kama hamaltahu alalladhina min qablina. Rabbana wa la tuhammilna ma la taqata lana bih. Wa'fu anna waghfir lana warhamna. Anta mawlana fansurna alal-qawmil-kafirin.
items.meaning:
The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. All of them believe in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers, saying: we make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: we hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return.

Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned, and against it is what it earned. Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay on us a burden like the one You laid on those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with more than we can bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so help us against the people who reject the truth.
items.when: At night, and it is enough to recite them in bed. Whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him.
items.virtue: They are from a treasure under the Throne, and Allah answered each asking in them. Whoever recites them at night, they suffice him.
items.reference: Qur'an 2:285-286. Sahih al-Bukhari 5009 and 5040; Sahih Muslim 807 and 808

items.title: I seek Allah's forgiveness, three times
items.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
items.transliteration: Astaghfirullah.
items.meaning: I seek the forgiveness of Allah.
items.when: Three times, right after the salam of the obligatory prayer, before the other adhkar.
items.virtue: Thawban said the Prophet ﷺ used to seek forgiveness three times when he finished the prayer, then say the next dua.

items.title: O Allah, You are Peace
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ، تَبَارَكْتَ يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ
items.transliteration: Allahumma Antas-Salamu wa minkas-salam, tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram.
items.meaning: O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor.
items.when: Once, immediately after the three istighfar, after every obligatory prayer.
items.virtue: The first long remembrance after the salam.

items.title: None can withhold what You give
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. اللَّهُمَّ لَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، وَلَا مُعْطِيَ لِمَا مَنَعْتَ، وَلَا يَنْفَعُ ذَا الْجَدِّ مِنْكَ الْجَدُّ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir. Allahumma la mani'a lima a'tayt, wa la mu'tiya lima mana't, wa la yanfa'u dhal-jaddi minkal-jadd.
items.meaning: There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and the wealth of a wealthy person is of no avail against You.
items.when: Once after every obligatory prayer. After Maghrib and Fajr, some narrations add the ten-times card as well.
items.virtue: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah said the Prophet ﷺ used to say this after every obligatory prayer.

items.title: Help me to remember You
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ
items.transliteration: Allahumma a'inni ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni ibadatik.
items.meaning: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well.
items.when: Mu'adh ibn Jabal was told to say it at the end of every prayer, and he was told not to leave it.
items.virtue: A small sentence that asks for the whole of worship.

items.title: Subhanallah, thirty-three times
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ
items.transliteration: Subhanallah.
items.meaning: Glory be to Allah.
items.when: After every obligatory prayer, as the first third of the tasbih. Then Alhamdulillah thirty-three, then Allahu Akbar thirty-four, or the form in the next cards.
items.virtue: The poor Muhajirun asked for a share in the reward of those who give charity. He taught them this tasbih after every prayer, and said it fills the gap.

items.title: Alhamdulillah, thirty-three times
items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
items.transliteration: Alhamdulillah.
items.meaning: Praise belongs to Allah.
items.when: After Subhanallah, thirty-three times, after every obligatory prayer.
items.virtue: Part of the same tasbih that the Prophet ﷺ compared to a charity the poor could give.

items.title: Allahu Akbar, thirty-four times
items.arabic: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
items.transliteration: Allahu Akbar.
items.meaning: Allah is greatest.
items.when: After the thirty-three praises and the thirty-three glorifications. Another sahih form is thirty-three of each, then the tahli once to complete one hundred. Both forms are sound.
items.virtue: Ka'b ibn Ujrah reported the thirty-four takbirs at the end.

items.title: The phrase that completes one hundred
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir.
items.meaning: There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things.
items.when: Once, after thirty-three Subhanallah, thirty-three Alhamdulillah, and thirty-three Allahu Akbar, if you are using the form that completes one hundred with this sentence.
items.virtue: His sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea.

items.title: Ayat al-Kursi after the obligatory prayer
items.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
items.transliteration: Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum. La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm. Lahu ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard. Man dhalladhi yashfa'u indahu illa bi-idhnih. Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum. Wa la yuhituna bi-shay'in min ilmihi illa bima sha'. Wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samawati wal-ard. Wa la ya'uduhu hifdhuhuma. Wa Huwal-Aliyyul-Azim.
items.meaning: Ayat al-Kursi, in full. The morning card carries the same English reading.
items.when: Once after each of the five obligatory prayers.
items.virtue: Nothing stands between him and Paradise except death. That is the report recorded by an-Nasa'i in al-Kubra and graded sahih by a number of hadith scholars.
items.reference: Qur'an 2:255; Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, from Abu Umamah

items.title: In Your name I die and I live
items.arabic: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا
items.transliteration: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya.
items.meaning: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
items.when: When you lie down to sleep. Hudhayfah said this is what the Prophet ﷺ said when he went to his bed.
items.virtue: Sleep is a small death. The dua places it in Allah's name.

items.title: Praise to the One who gave us life again
items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
items.transliteration: Alhamdu lillahilladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.
items.meaning: Praise belongs to Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.
items.when: As soon as you wake.
items.virtue: The pair of the sleep dua. Hudhayfah reported both.

items.title: The three surahs, then wipe the body
items.arabic:
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ۝ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ۝ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ۝ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ۝ وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ۝ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ۝ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ۝ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ۝ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
items.transliteration: Qul Huwallahu Ahad. Allahus-Samad. Lam yalid wa lam yulad. Wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad. Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbil-falaq, min sharri ma khalaq, wa min sharri ghasqin idha waqab, wa min sharrin-naffathati fil-uqad, wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad. Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbin-nas, Malikin-nas, Ilahin-nas, min sharril-waswasil-khannas, alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas, minal-jinnati wan-nas.
items.meaning: Say the three surahs in full: Allah is One, the Eternal Refuge, with none equal to Him. Seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak from created evil, from darkness, from those who blow on knots, and from the envier. Seek refuge in the Lord of mankind from the retreating whisperer among jinn and people.
items.when: When you are in bed. Cup your hands, recite the three surahs, blow lightly into your hands, and wipe whatever you can of your body, starting with the head and face and the front of the body. Do that three times.
items.virtue: Aishah said the Prophet ﷺ did this every night when he went to his bed, and that in his final illness she did it for him and he wiped with her hands, hoping for their blessing.

items.title: Ayat al-Kursi before sleep
items.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
items.transliteration: Allahu la ilaha illa Huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum. La ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm. Lahu ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard. Man dhalladhi yashfa'u indahu illa bi-idhnih. Ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum. Wa la yuhituna bi-shay'in min ilmihi illa bima sha'. Wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samawati wal-ard. Wa la ya'uduhu hifdhuhuma. Wa Huwal-Aliyyul-Azim.
items.meaning: Allah, there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. No one intercedes except by His permission. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and guarding them does not tire Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
items.when: Once, when you lie down.
items.virtue: A protector from Allah stays over you, and shaytan does not approach you until morning. Abu Hurayrah learned this from the devil who had come as a thief, and the Prophet ﷺ said Abu Hurayrah had told the truth, though he is a liar.

items.title: I have submitted my face to You
items.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ، وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ، وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ، رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ، لَا مَلْجَأَ وَلَا مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلَّا إِلَيْكَ، اللَّهُمَّ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ، وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ
items.transliteration: Allahumma aslamtu wajhi ilayk, wa fawwadtu amri ilayk, wa alja'tu dhahri ilayk, raghbatan wa rahbatan ilayk. La malja'a wa la manja minka illa ilayk. Allahumma amantu bi-kitabikal-ladhi anzalt, wa bi-nabiyyikal-ladhi arsalt.
items.meaning: O Allah, I have submitted my face to You, entrusted my affair to You, and laid my back against You, in hope of You and in fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. O Allah, I believe in Your Book which You sent down, and in Your Prophet whom You sent.
items.when: When you go to bed, perform wudu as for the prayer, lie on your right side, and make these the last words you say. Al-Bara' repeated it back and said 'Your messenger' instead of 'Your prophet.' The Prophet ﷺ corrected him: say nabiyyika, Your prophet.
items.virtue: He told al-Bara' to repeat it back, and he corrected him when he said 'Your messenger' instead of 'Your prophet.' Keep the wording nabiyyika.

items.title: When you put your hand under your cheek
items.arabic: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَضَعْتُ جَنْبِي، وَبِكَ أَرْفَعُهُ، إِنْ أَمْسَكْتَ نَفْسِي فَارْحَمْهَا، وَإِنْ أَرْسَلْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا بِمَا تَحْفَظُ بِهِ عِبَادَكَ الصَّالِحِينَ
items.transliteration: Bismika Allahumma wada'tu janbi, wa bika arfa'uh. In amsakta nafsi farhamha, wa in arsaltaha fahfazha bima tahfazu bihi ibadakas-salihin.
items.meaning: In Your name, O Allah, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You hold my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, guard it with what You guard Your righteous servants.
items.when: Lying on the right side, with the hand under the cheek. A shorter report is: Allahumma qini adhabaka yawma tab'athu ibadak.
items.virtue: Hudhayfah and al-Bara' both describe his sleep adab. The short refuge from the punishment of the Day he raises His servants is in Sunan Abi Dawud 5045.
items.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6313 for this longer wording; Sunan Abi Dawud 5045 for the shorter one

items.title: The tasbih of Fatimah before sleep
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ ٣٣، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٣٣، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ ٣٤
items.transliteration: Subhanallah thirty-three, Alhamdulillah thirty-three, Allahu Akbar thirty-four.
items.meaning: Glory be to Allah. Praise belongs to Allah. Allah is greatest.
items.when: Before sleep, when the work of the house is done. Ali and Fatimah asked for a servant. He taught them this instead, and said it is better for them than a servant. The counter here tracks one hundred phrases: 33, then 33, then 34.
items.virtue: Ali said: I did not leave it since the day I heard it. He was asked about the night of Siffin and said he remembered it even then.
items.note: Count 33, then 33, then 34. The button simply keeps a running total to 100.

items.title: There is no power except with Allah
items.arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
items.transliteration: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
items.meaning: There is no power and no strength except with Allah.
items.when: Throughout the day, especially when a task feels heavy, and after the mu'adhdhin says Hayya alas-salah and Hayya alal-falah. At those two lines the listener says this instead of repeating him.
items.virtue: It is a plant in Paradise, and a treasure among the treasures of Paradise.

items.title: The four words most loved by Allah
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
items.transliteration: Subhanallah, walhamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar.
items.meaning: Glory be to Allah, praise belongs to Allah, there is no god except Allah, and Allah is greatest.
items.when: Any time. Samurah ibn Jundub reported that they are the most beloved speech to Allah.
items.virtue: Four words. No count was fixed. Say them often.

items.title: Two words, heavy on the Scale
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
items.transliteration: Subhanallahi wa bihamdih, Subhanallahil-Azim.
items.meaning: Glory and praise be to Allah. Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent.
items.when: Any time, as often as the tongue is free.
items.virtue: Two phrases that are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful.

items.title: Glory and praise, one hundred times
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
items.transliteration: Subhanallahi wa bihamdih.
items.meaning: Glory and praise be to Allah.
items.when: One hundred times in the day. The morning is a good place for it, and any hour counts.
items.virtue: His sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea. Whoever says it one hundred times in the morning and one hundred times in the evening, no one will bring better on the Day of Resurrection except someone who said the same or more.

items.title: La ilaha illallah, one hundred times
items.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
items.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ala kulli shay'in Qadir.
items.meaning: There is no god except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and the praise, and He is able to do all things.
items.when: One hundred times in the day.
items.virtue: It is equal to freeing ten slaves, one hundred good deeds are written, one hundred sins are erased, it is a protection from shaytan for that day until evening, and no one brings better except someone who did more.

items.title: I seek forgiveness and I repent
items.arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
items.transliteration: Astaghfirullaha wa atubu ilayh.
items.meaning: I seek the forgiveness of Allah and I repent to Him.
items.when: Through the day. He ﷺ used to seek forgiveness more than seventy times, and in a gathering more than one hundred times, while his past and future sins were already forgiven.
items.virtue: If he did that, the rest of us have more reason. The count of one hundred follows the gathering in which Abu Hurayrah heard him pass one hundred.

items.title: Glory as many times as His creation
items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، عَدَدَ خَلْقِهِ، وَرِضَا نَفْسِهِ، وَزِنَةَ عَرْشِهِ، وَمِدَادَ كَلِمَاتِهِ
items.transliteration: Subhanallahi wa bihamdih, adada khalqih, wa rida nafsih, wa zinata arshih, wa midada kalimatih.
items.meaning: Glory and praise be to Allah, as many times as His creation, as much as pleases Him, as heavy as His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words.
items.when: Three times. Juwayriyah was still on her morning tasbih when he left and when he returned at mid-morning. He taught her these words, said three times, and told her they outweigh everything she had been saying since the morning.
items.virtue: A short dhikr with a vast meaning. Say it with attention, not as a trick to skip remembrance.
